task.name: Diagnose treats a missing agent result as malformed and retries reformatting nothing
task.story_text:
## Observed

Ran `forge diagnose --verbose --issue 437,435,431 --parallel 3` on v0.16.0rc14
against an adopter repo. One of the three runs ended at PARSE:

```
PARSE failed: investigative agent did not emit a parseable YAML block (YAML
block did not parse to a mapping of diagnosis keys (root was str).) and 2
reformat retry attempt(s) did not produce one.
Raw tail: "I'll wait for the actual completion notification from the
investigation agent rather than polling further."
```

The audit records `final_phase: FAILED`, `agent.reported_success: false`,
`agent.failure_code: null`, cost $0.49, duration 65s. The agent's final output
is a statement that it is waiting for a sub-investigation to report back; it
ends without ever producing a result block of any kind. Both reformat retries
ran against that same output, so each retry was asked to reformat something
that was absent rather than malformed. Nothing landed and the issue remains at
`needs_diagnosis`.

Audit: `.forge/audits/diagnose-issue-431-3ff52d649fe5.yaml`, with the agent
output captured alongside it as `.raw.txt`, `.raw.retry1.txt` and
`.raw.retry2.txt`.

## Expected

A diagnose run should end either with a result the flow can parse or with a
failure that names why the result is absent, and those two situations should be
distinguishable without opening the raw output. Output that is malformed and
output that was never produced are different conditions: reformatting can
recover the first and can never recover the second, so retrying the reformat
step against an empty result repeats a step that cannot succeed and spends
budget doing it.

Separately, an agent that hands part of its work to a sub-investigation should
not be able to terminate while still waiting on that work. Whatever mechanism
returns a sub-investigation's result to its caller should either deliver it or
surface its absence as the reason the run failed, so that a run which stops
early is reported as an incomplete delegation rather than as an unparseable
result.

## Diagnosis

**Baseline:** `27a1b77f330ba34f94c0dc5bc81fe01bec03c035` captured at `2026-09-04T15:26:27.684381+00:00`

**Inspected files:**

- `src/theforge/coordinator/diagnose_flow.py` — `sha256:ea674a37a2776bb406c76e9b1d0341343585d7b9acd8b35c4d32e6704c1aa441`
- `src/theforge/runners/runner_claude.py` — `sha256:e12e43be829b94f8f22dcb4e3873ee124795031f4f42c36720b4992bb06070dc`
- `src/theforge/agent_types.py` — `sha256:f25462e523ec3718ede9cca8a60ea5f242c1451301d2ec84f77b2c97c8880217`
- `tests/test_diagnose_parse_retry.py` — `sha256:aeba88718b287e5a63b0efdeff2bd1ef16b2970fe0166e200148694f9f52ac2f`

### Observed symptom

Content class: confirmed symptom/evidence.
A `forge diagnose` run whose investigative agent delegated part of its work
to a sub-investigation and ended its billed turn on a status line stating it
was still waiting for that work, without ever emitting a diagnosis result
block, was not classified by the coordinator's dedicated
"delegated_without_observed_outcome" failure path. Instead it fell through
to the reformat-retry path, spent two retry invocations attempting to
reformat output that was never a completed diagnosis, and ended as an
opaque "PARSE failed ... did not emit a parseable YAML block" error with
`agent.failure_code: null`, leaving the issue at `needs_diagnosis`.

### Reproduction / evidence

Content class: confirmed symptom/evidence.
Cited from the issue: `forge diagnose --verbose --issue 437,435,431 --parallel 3`
on v0.16.0rc14 produced audit `.forge/audits/diagnose-issue-431-3ff52d649fe5.yaml`
with `final_phase: FAILED`, `agent.reported_success: false`,
`agent.failure_code: null`, cost $0.49, duration 65s, and raw-output tail
"I'll wait for the actual completion notification from the investigation
agent rather than polling further." That specific audit/raw-output bundle
is not present in this checkout (it belongs to the reporting adopter's own
`.forge/` tree), so this diagnosis was built by reading this repository's
current source at HEAD (27a1b77f) and confirming every quoted field value
is produced by, and only by, one specific code path, plus running the
exact quoted phrasing through the detector's own regex patterns by
inspection.

### Hypotheses tested

- **[confirmed]** The delegated-placeholder detector's `result.success` guard disqualifies this exact run shape (real placeholder output, but `success=False`), so it never gets to inspect the output/tool_trace and the flow falls through to reformat retries.
  - Evidence: diagnose_flow.py:158 is `if not bool(getattr(result, "success", False)): return ""` — the very first statement in `_ended_on_delegated_waiting_placeholder`, before any output/tool_trace inspection. runner_claude.py:1171-1196 is the branch taken when the CLI stream *did* contain a terminal `type: result` event (the `if not result_json:` guard at line 1098 is false), and its `AgentResult(...)` call at line 1182-1196 sets `success=proc.returncode == 0` (line 1183) while passing no `failure_code=` keyword at all — `AgentResult.failure_code` (agent_types.py:171) defaults to `None`. That combination — a captured real result-event `output` (line 1184, `result_json.get("result")` verbatim), `success=False` on nonzero exit, and `failure_code=None` — reproduces every field the issue's audit quotes. Contrast with the sibling 'no result event at all' branch (lines 1149-1152), which *does* set `failure_code=FAILURE_ENDED_WITHOUT_RESULT` on nonzero exit — so the issue's `failure_code: null` specifically rules out that branch and confirms the result-event branch (1171-1196) was taken, i.e. the agent's placeholder text was real, complete output, not a truncated stream.
  - Claim verification: verified against the target repository source. Read diagnose_flow.py:87-172 (detector + patterns) and :1879-1918 (call site and fallthrough to _retry_diagnose_parse), runner_claude.py:1090-1196 (both AgentResult return branches) and agent_types.py:171 (failure_code default) directly in this checkout at HEAD.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. All cited line numbers and code substrings were read directly from the repository at commit 27a1b77f during this investigation. The specific field values ($0.49, 65s, failure_code: null, raw tail text) are taken from the issue body's quoted audit, which could not be independently re-opened in this checkout.
- **[confirmed]** Even if `success` had been True, the existing waiting/deferred -outcome regexes do not match this run's exact phrasing, so the text-only fallback path would also have missed this case.
  - Evidence: Applying `_WAITING_PLACEHOLDER_PATTERNS` and `_DEFERRED_OUTCOME_PATTERNS` (diagnose_flow.py:89-102) to the quoted text "I'll wait for the actual completion notification from the investigation agent rather than polling further": the second waiting pattern requires 'wait(?:ing)? for the' to be immediately followed by 'investigation/exploration/sub-agent', but here it is followed by 'actual completion notification from the' — no match. No deferred -outcome pattern ('report...once/when', 'no need to poll', '.../to follow') matches either. `_TEXT_ONLY_DELEGATION_PATTERNS` does match ('investigation agent' appears), so `mentions_delegated_agent` is True, but `_has_delegated_placeholder_signal` is False, and `_ended_on_delegated_waiting_placeholder` requires both — so the text-only fallback returns "" for this exact wording even under `success=True`.
  - Claim verification: verified against the target repository source. Applied each compiled regex in diagnose_flow.py:89-111 against the quoted raw-tail string by direct inspection of the pattern definitions read from the file at HEAD.
  - Evidence provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. Regex source and match analysis performed directly in this investigation against the file at HEAD.
- **[unverifiable]** The tool-trace path (`_delegation_tools_used`) might have independently caught this run via a recorded Agent/ScheduleWakeup tool call, bypassing the phrasing gap in hypothesis 2 — but cannot salvage the run either way, because it sits behind the same `result.success` guard as hypothesis 1.
  - Evidence: Whether this specific run's tool_trace contains an agent/schedulewakeup entry is unknown — the run's audit/raw-output bundle is not present in this checkout, only the issue's summary of it. This does not affect the confirmed cause: the success guard at diagnose_flow.py:158 disqualifies the tool-trace path exactly the same way it disqualifies the text-only path, regardless of what the trace contains.
  - Claim verification: rests only on attached evidence. Would require the original .raw.txt/audit YAML (not present in this checkout) to check the recorded tool_trace; not needed to confirm hypothesis 1, which fully explains the observed field values independent of tool_trace contents.
  - Evidence provenance: unknown — the diagnosis did not record whether this support was directly observed or read as a prior assertion. Tool trace contents for this specific run are not available locally; this sub-question was not resolved either way.

### Confirmed cause

Content class: confirmed localization.
`_ended_on_delegated_waiting_placeholder` in
`src/theforge/coordinator/diagnose_flow.py` requires `result.success` to be
True before it will classify a run as an incomplete delegation
(`diagnose_flow.py:158`). The Claude runner's "CLI emitted a terminal
result event" return branch (`runner_claude.py:1171-1196`) sets
`success = (process exit code == 0)` independently of whether that result
event carried real, complete output text, and in that specific branch it
passes no `failure_code` argument to `AgentResult` at all, so
`failure_code` defaults to `None`. A run whose CLI process exits nonzero
after streaming a genuine terminal result event — including one whose text
is a delegation-waiting placeholder — therefore produces exactly the
tuple `success=False, failure_code=None, output=<real placeholder text>`.
Because the detector's guard clause treats `success=False` as disqualifying
before it ever looks at `output` or `tool_trace`, this shape is invisible
to the delegation detector and falls through to `_retry_diagnose_parse`
(`diagnose_flow.py:1906-1918`), which spends the configured reformat-retry
budget (2 retries here) attempting to reformat content that was never a
completed diagnosis, then reports a generic `PARSE failed` error instead
of naming the delegation as the reason the run failed.

Claim verification: verified against the target repository source. Both halves of the mechanism (the detector's success guard and the runner's success/failure_code assignment in both AgentResult return branches) were read directly from diagnose_flow.py, runner_claude.py, and agent_types.py at HEAD (27a1b77f) in this checkout. The regex non-match for the exact quoted phrasing was verified by direct pattern inspection. The specific field values quoted from the failing run's audit were not independently re-opened locally (that audit is not present in this checkout) but are consistent with, and only with, this code path.
Support: Content class: confirmed localization support.
Two independently-read facts compose to reproduce every field the issue's
audit quotes: (1) `diagnose_flow.py:158`'s `if not bool(getattr(result,
"success", False)): return ""` is the first statement of the detector
function, executed before any inspection of `output` or `tool_trace`; (2)
`runner_claude.py:1183` sets `success=proc.returncode == 0` inside the
branch reached only when a genuine `type: result` event was found in the
CLI's stream (guard `if not result_json:` at line 1098 is false), and that
branch's `AgentResult(...)` call (lines 1182-1196) has no `failure_code=`
keyword, so it defaults to `None` per `agent_types.py:171`. The sibling
"no result event" branch (`runner_claude.py:1149-1152`) explicitly sets
`failure_code=FAILURE_ENDED_WITHOUT_RESULT` on nonzero exit, which the
issue's `failure_code: null` rules out — pinning the failing run to the
result-event branch, i.e. confirming the agent's placeholder text was real
captured output, not a truncated/killed stream. This is a first-hand
reading of the current source, not a restatement of a prior conclusion:
issue #2887's own diagnosis section contained this same analysis before I
began, but I re-derived and independently checked each cited line and
regex against the file contents at HEAD rather than trusting that text.
Support provenance: observed — directly observed during this investigation. All line numbers, code substrings, and regex-match analysis were read and performed directly against the repository at HEAD during this investigation. The issue body already contained a diagnosis section stating the same conclusion when I started; I treated that as an unverified prior draft and re-derived every claim independently from source rather than citing it as corroboration.
Independence note: This text uses independence/corroboration language. Verify the cited material is a second source rather than a prior assertion.

### Affected code path

Content class: confirmed localization.
src/theforge/coordinator/diagnose_flow.py:158 (`_ended_on_delegated_waiting_placeholder`'s
`result.success` guard) and its call site at diagnose_flow.py:1890-1918
(fallthrough to `_retry_diagnose_parse` when the detector returns "");
src/theforge/runners/runner_claude.py:1182-1196 (`AgentResult(success=proc.returncode
== 0, ...)` with no `failure_code` set, in the branch reached when a
genuine terminal result event was captured).

### Fix-success criterion

Content class: behavioral requirement for the eventual fix.
A diagnose run whose investigative agent's captured output is real,
non-empty, and reads as an unresolved delegation (by the existing
text/tool-trace heuristics) is classified as
`delegated_without_observed_outcome` and skips reformat retries,
regardless of whether the runner's `success` flag is True or False for
that turn — i.e., the detector's classification depends on "did this turn
produce real, complete output that reads as an unresolved delegation," not
on the runner's process-exit-code-derived success flag. A run matching
this issue's exact quoted symptom must end with
`failure_code: delegated_without_observed_outcome` and zero reformat-retry
attempts, not a `PARSE failed` message.

### Related findings (out of scope)

> These are adjacent problems noticed during investigation. They are **not** the cause of this issue's symptom and are **out of scope for this fix** — triage them separately under the linked issue. Do not implement them as part of this issue.

- The waiting/deferred-outcome regex set is narrow and phrasing-brittle (confirmed in hypothesis 2): even independent of the success-guard bug, wording drift in the investigative agent's own phrasing can silently defeat the text-only fallback. This is a robustness gap in the same detector, not a distinct root cause of this issue's reported symptom. (related: #2887)

### Advisory repair proposal

> Advisory only: this is an unverified repair idea from the investigation, not part of the confirmed diagnosis contract.

Two independently-fixable gaps compose to produce this symptom; a fix
should likely address both: (1) drop or loosen the `result.success` guard
in `_ended_on_delegated_waiting_placeholder` so it inspects `output`/
`tool_trace` regardless of the runner's success flag — the function's own
docstring already targets "a billed top-level turn that delegated and
stopped on a status line," and a nonzero exit code doesn't change that the
text is real, unresolved delegation output; (2) broaden
`_WAITING_PLACEHOLDER_PATTERNS`/`_DEFERRED_OUTCOME_PATTERNS` (or add a new
pattern) to cover phrasing like "wait for the actual completion
notification ... rather than polling further," since even a
`success=True` run with this exact wording currently slips past the
text-only fallback too. A fix should re-run
`tests/test_diagnose_parse_retry.py`'s existing delegation tests (all of
which construct their fake result with the test helper's `success=True`
default — none exercise `success=False` with real placeholder output) and
add a case combining `success=False` with this issue's literal wording.

### Notes

I could not locate or open the specific audit/raw-output files this issue
quotes (`.forge/audits/diagnose-issue-431-3ff52d649fe5.yaml`, `.raw.txt`,
`.raw.retry1.txt`, `.raw.retry2.txt`) in this checkout — they belong to the
reporting adopter's own `.forge/` tree, not this repository's. This
diagnosis is built entirely from reading this repository's current source
(diagnose_flow.py, runner_claude.py, agent_types.py, and
tests/test_diagnose_parse_retry.py) at HEAD and checking that every field
value the issue quotes is produced by, and only by, the identified code
path. The issue's second ask — "whatever mechanism returns a
sub-investigation's result to its caller should either deliver it or
surface its absence" — concerns the sub-agent delivery/notification
plumbing an investigative CLI session itself uses (e.g. the Agent-tool /
ScheduleWakeup notification path), which is outside theforge's own
coordinator/runner code and outside what this investigation could verify
in this repository; I scoped `confirmed_cause` to the forge-side
classification gap only, which is the part reproducible from this
codebase and squarely a theforge bug regardless of how that underlying
delivery mechanism behaves. The issue body already contained a fully
written diagnosis section when I began this run; I treated it as an
unverified prior draft, not as evidence, and independently re-derived
every cited line, regex match, and field-value correspondence directly
against the source at HEAD before confirming the same conclusion.
